scheduler.title: Replay Schedule Watch
scheduler.prompt:
Audit scheduled replay liveness for ryansctt1994-sudo/introspection-twin. GitHub main, pull requests, workflows and operational replay policies are read-only: do not merge PRs, modify those policies, rerun workflows, or post GitHub comments/messages. The only authorized remote writes are monitor-heartbeat documents on the dedicated monitor/replay-heartbeats branch and signed monitor-heartbeat entries in public Rekor.

Read the committed main-branch .github/replay-schedule.json, .github/workflows/ci.yml, and docs/evidence/SCHEDULE_LIVENESS_2026-11-04.md. Confirm PR #12 is merged before treating that policy as deployed. The initial daily expectation is 15:47 UTC, arrival by 16:07 UTC and completion by 16:27 UTC, starting 2026-11-04. Audit each elapsed expected slot since the last recorded audit; on the first invocation audit from 2026-11-04. Retain a cursor and per-slot JSON receipts in /workspace/replay-schedule-monitor if a workspace is available; also include the audited date range in your result so subsequent invocations can recover if workspace files are missing. Never silently skip an unaudited day or erase a missed window after late success.

Use connected GitHub tools to read workflow state and actual schedule-event runs for workflow ID 374465172 on main, with complete pagination. The repo's scripts/check_schedule_liveness.py is usable against the public read-only API in a managed environment, but fetch it from the committed main version and record its source SHA and policy hash. If the environment is unavailable use connected tools and the same committed rules. Missing or disabled workflows, absent runs past the arrival deadline, late arrivals, failed runs, and incomplete runs past the completion deadline are findings. API failures, missing coverage, malformed records or ambiguous reruns are INCONCLUSIVE, never healthy. A push, pull_request, workflow_dispatch, or historical rerun cannot substitute for a newly scheduled event. Inspect the GitHub-hosted watchdog too. Its 16:29 UTC trigger has a 20-minute arrival grace and a 25-minute completion grace (16:49 and 16:54 UTC). Its absence or unfinished run past those deadlines is a separate finding, not a reason to stay silent.

For a genuine candidate scheduled run, inspect its jobs and raw logs/trigger-record.json: exact event and cron, source SHA/tree, fresh_requested=true, fresh_verified=true, zero fresh checker and fresh-log tee exits and zero outer replay/tee exits, real checker diagnostics, and final observed replay receipt. Distinguish schedule occurrence/completion metadata from fully checked FRESH replay evidence. Creation-time windows and cron strings do not prove the original intended date for a very delayed daily event; report attribution uncertainty. Record failures with links and observation times. Keep the original 14:45 UTC miss as a separate historical finding with its explicitly retrospective threshold.

Report a concise dated status and evidence links to me, including the first qualified scheduled FRESH run if one exists. Say explicitly if qualification remains missing. This task is externally scheduled relative to GitHub Actions but operates under the same owner/principal; do not label it independent witnessing or guaranteed availability. If this monitor itself runs late, name that gap. No other queued project work is authorized within this monitoring task.

Historical baseline already verified in the source conversation: genuine schedule run 41857790032 on merged #11 source 3b811cd008495b51c75f9d942b04a440580c1d88 passed FRESH=1 with actual checker diagnostics and zero checker/logger exits. It was created 2026-11-04T15:26:37Z, before the new daily slot, and did not record its exact cron. Preserve that historical qualification; do not count it for a later slot or erase the earlier missed window. PR #12 subsequently merged at 64b89a5dc73a42fd062370178ffb62bb4f028187.

Public monitor timestamp and heartbeat requirement (authorized 2026-11-06):
At the very start, record intended_fire_time and actual_arrival_time separately in UTC for this monitor execution. actual_arrival_time is the first observed assistant audit clock reading; identify that provenance explicitly. Preserve scheduler scheduled_for/started_at if available and its reported last_run_time separately. Missing detailed run/delivery history is unknown, not evidence of execution. Do not infer the original intended date of a very delayed invocation solely from its arrival time. If intended slot attribution is ambiguous, expose null/unknown and the candidate slots rather than inventing one. Always show the two raw timestamps in the user report so lateness can be recomputed. Preserve existing receipts; use append-only timestamp annotations/inventories instead of rewriting historical receipt bytes.

After EVERY monitor execution, including an INCONCLUSIVE audit, publish one canonical signed public heartbeat and its audit receipt digest. Publish files only under monitor-heartbeats/ on branch monitor/replay-heartbeats in ryansctt1994-sudo/introspection-twin. Do not touch main/workflow/replay-policy files. Use commit messages containing [skip ci] so heartbeat publication does not trigger Actions. Give each execution a unique date/audit-ID directory and retain every earlier publication, failure and late deadline. Include previous heartbeat digest/Rekor entry where available. Sign and anchor the heartbeat in https://rekor.sigstore.dev, verify inclusion, pinned log key, public readback, author-key match, and a separately fetched service-owned signed checkpoint connected by a verified consistency proof (publisher.live_log), then publish the proof files and latest pointer. A hash-only entry with no retrievable public payload is missing coverage. Record publication failures as HEARTBEAT_PUBLICATION_FAILED/INCONCLUSIVE; never claim a heartbeat was posted without verified evidence.

Frozen public cadence manifest: monitor-heartbeats/cadence.json on that branch, SHA-256 6f9932dab0e6e165f40c9109ea8d0304b8443702ff8a5c17281b37262aef517f. Its prospective first slot is 2026-11-07T16:57:00Z; daily intended fire is 16:57 UTC, and heartbeat publication is due by 17:17 UTC. This adds a publication expectation; it does not reschedule the task or change GitHub policy. Missing publication after the deadline or late Rekor integratedTime is a preserved finding even after late success. The November 6 heartbeat is retrospective bootstrap, not a backdated on-time result. Bootstrap Rekor entry: https://rekor.sigstore.dev/api/v1/log/entries/108e9186e8c5677a383079d2e9c69de9cf72668924747dac6d94459e16509e0b626a1d0ad4a08483 .

Existing local private-key path, if available: /workspace/replay-schedule-monitor/private/heartbeat-author.pem . Never print or publish that private key, silently replace it, or generate a different agent/key and call it independent. If unavailable, retain the failed publication finding; recover the public cadence/history and report the key-custody gap. Publisher/verifier reference sources are under monitor-heartbeats/publisher/ on the public branch; fetch/review the committed files rather than assuming a previous workspace exists. Use the frozen public pins, not new values supplied by an incoming payload. The payload must carry intended/actual timestamps, provenance, publication preparation time, audited date range, source/policy hashes, audit receipt digest, current findings, and a public verification location. Rekor's integratedTime proves publication time only: it does not certify the claimed arrival time, execution, findings, independent witnessing, or guaranteed availability.
